prerequisites: Analysis, calculation and evaluation of component stresses, especially surface pressure, bending, Mohr's stress circle, combined stresses, cutting principle, forces, transverse contraction, shear, buckling.

Fundamentals of statics, mechanical modeling, analysis and calculation of acting forces and moments, structure of statically determinate structures, calculation and evaluation of static stress on components.

Fundamentals of materials science, properties of metallic materials and relationship between microstructure and macroscopic material parameters, structure of metallic materials, material behavior, iron-carbon diagram, heat treatments and TTT diagrams, steel designations, properties and material behavior of iron-based materials and material selection.
Knowledge, selection and ability to calculate connecting elements, especially bolts, pins, soldered, glued, and welded joints, shaft-hub connections and screw connections.
Fundamentals of component modeling and drawing creation.
Performing strength calculations and proofs, especially on the aforementioned machine elements.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can classify the various gear elements.
They are able to represent them themselves in technical drawings and know their function and structure.
They also master basic design rules for the use of gear elements and are able to determine essential calculation factors themselves with the help of diagrams and formulas.
They can assess the relevance of calculation factors for the respective load case.
They know the basic stress types and frequently occurring failure modes of gear elements, as well as their effects on dimensioning and design.
Furthermore, students are able to make initial sensible assumptions for the design of gears/gear elements with the help of design calculations.
In particular, students can identify critical cross-sections for gearings and shafts/axles and perform corresponding strength verifications.
They are generally able to perform and evaluate strength verifications on mechanical engineering parts.
They are able to create their own designs of shafts and axles for the respective application.
They can also design and calculate shafts and axles.
They are able to distinguish between different types of gears and can evaluate gear designs in terms of their quality.
Students can select suitable plain and rolling bearings for the respective application and perform corresponding service life verifications.
They can name the different types of gearing and explain how gearings work.
They know how the basic tooth form can be geometrically generated.
They are able to calculate the geometric parameters for spur gears themselves.
They are able to design, dimension and recalculate gear connections.
For this purpose, they master common failure cases in gearings and can determine forces and strength parameters in gearings.
Students are able to design, dimension, recalculate and evaluate positive and non-positive form and position tolerances.

syllabus_topics: Axles and shafts: Function, design, draft and strength calculation
Geometry and strength of spur gearing
assessment_rules: To receive credit points, the module examination must be passed and a performance record must be provided. The weighting of the grade for the final grade is according to the study and examination regulations (SPO).
